newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army breaks up Uprona party meeting.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army breaks up Uprona party meeting.

text.p: Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army on Wednesday broke up a meeting of the Uprona party, which opposes a government strategy of negotiating with Hutu rebels, witnesses said.
Around 100 soldiers raided Uprona party headquarters in the capital and ejected party chairman Charles Mukasi and Bujumbura party bosses.
"They stopped me from holding the meeting and they have denied me any freedom," Mukasi said by telephone. He said the government had told Uprona party branches to sideline him.
There was no comment from the government.
Uprona, widely seen as a pro-Tutsi party, opposes negotiations as "high treason", arguing it is inappropriate with a group accused of genocide.
The army raided Mukasi's residence this month.
Burundi military leader Pierre Buyoya announced in May negotiations between the government and the National Council for the Defence of Democracy, the main Hutu rebel group.
More than 150,000 people have died in Burundi since 1993 when Tutsi troops murdered Melchior Ndadaye, the country's first freely-elected Hutu president.
